title: Composition of normalized scalar arrows
statement: Let a:Λ0→Λ1, b:Λ1→Λ2 and c:Λ0→Λ2 be commutative condensed ring-object maps with a≫b=c. For any scheme X form the exact restriction compositor from Mod.comapComp and coefficientMap_comp, and let A:Lc≅La⋙Lb be its conjugate under the actual derived scalar adjunctions of [def-sfb-diagonal-coefficient-endpoints]. For modules M0,M1,M2 and Semilinear structures s01,s12,s02 whose underlying maps satisfy m01≫m12=m02, write scalarHom for the transpose of the single of s.hom followed by the inverse exact restriction/single comparison. Then scalarHom(c,s02)=A_M0≫Lb(scalarHom(a,s01))≫scalarHom(b,s12). The same equation holds after shifting by two, using the left shifts induced by the actual scalar adjunctions. No invertibility, diagram, class, trace, direct-image or flatness assumption is required.

proof.text: Construct exact restriction composition by localizing inverse Mod.comapComp followed by comapCongr for coefficientMap_comp. Its left conjugate is the actual scalar associator. Faithfulness of module forgetting and the underlying composition equation identify the ordinary semilinear insertions.

Apply the proved exact-degree-zero adjointInsertion_comp to these three exact restriction functors and their actual scalar adjunctions. Its compositor is definitionally the one chosen here. Cancel the inverse left associator to obtain the unshifted equation.

The exact-derived natural-iso and composition comparisons commute with shifts, by the proved source instances in DerivedCategory.Shift.ExactFunctor. Expand inverse conjugation into units, counits, whiskerings and associators: each factor commutes with shifts because the left shifts are induced by the right adjoints. Shift the unshifted equation and use naturality of the second scalar functor shift comparison.

lean.statement:
theorem scalarHom_comp (hcoeff : a ≫ b = c) {X : Scheme.{u}}
    {M₀ : Modules Λ₀ X} {M₁ : Modules Λ₁ X} {M₂ : Modules Λ₂ X}
    {m₀₁ : M₀.X ⟶ M₁.X} {m₁₂ : M₁.X ⟶ M₂.X} {m₀₂ : M₀.X ⟶ M₂.X}
    (s₀₁ : Semilinear a M₀ M₁ m₀₁) (s₁₂ : Semilinear b M₁ M₂ m₁₂)
    (s₀₂ : Semilinear c M₀ M₂ m₀₂) (hline : m₀₁ ≫ m₁₂ = m₀₂) :
    (scalarHom c s₀₂ =
      (scalarCompIso a b c hcoeff X).hom.app _ ≫
        (derivedScalars b X).map (scalarHom a s₀₁) ≫ scalarHom b s₁₂) ∧
    (scalarShiftHom c s₀₂ =
      (scalarCompIso a b c hcoeff X).hom.app _ ≫
        (derivedScalars b X).map (scalarShiftHom a s₀₁) ≫ scalarShiftHom b s₁₂)
